questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

My father did not approve ______ the plan of travelling to Uttarakhand because of bad weather there.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer:** of 

‘approve of’ means ‘give consent or assent to something’. Therefore, it fits the context of the sentence in not giving consent to the plan of travelling to Uttarakhand.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P: Most of them are combinations of hydrogen and carbon in varying proportions.

Q: Crude mineral oil comes out of the earth as a thick brown or black liquid with a strong smell.

R: It is a complex mixture of many different substances, each with its own individual qualities.

S: Such hydrocarbons are also found in other forms such as bitumen, asphalt and natural gas.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: **QRPS

The first sentence must be Sentence Q, which introduces the crude mineral oils. It is followed by its definition, which is Sentence R. Also, it is clear that Sentence P must be followed by Sentence S, as P uses the word ‘carbon’ first. Therefore, the correct sequence is QRPS.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase.**

To steal a march

options.text: To act in a foolish way

questions.solution:
**Correct Answer**: To outshine 

‘To steal a march’ means to gain an advantage unexpectedly or secretly. From the given options, ‘to outshine’ is the closest in meaning and therefore, the correct answer.

An example sentence is: ‘The local retail store stole a march on the big brands during the sale time’.

questions.question: **In the following question, four words are given out of which one word is incorrectly ****spelt****. Select the incorrectly ****spelt**** word. **
questions.solution:

questions.question:

If it would (1)/rains they will (2)/not come. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer:** 1 

The sentence uses the tenses incorrectly, by using ‘would’ first, which is the past tense and then ‘will’.

Since the event of 'raining' is a conditional event, we use the simple present tense of the verb 'rain' in this case.

The correct sentence is: If it** rains**, they will not come.

• **Open: **Not closed, covered, or concealed; accessible to all; not secret or hidden (Hindi meaning: खुला)
 
• These two words are opposite because clandestine implies secrecy, concealment, and keeping things hidden, while open implies transparency, accessibility, and the absence of secrecy.
 
• Clandestine activities are intentionally kept hidden or private, whereas open activities are visible, accessible, and known to others.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Open**.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.**

The teacher said to the student, "Have you brought your lunch?"

options.text: The student was asked by the teacher about bringing his lunch.
The teacher asked the student if he would be bringing his lunch.
The teacher asked the student if he had brought his lunch.
The teacher asked the student if he has brought his lunch.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The teacher asked the student if he had brought his lunch.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in Direct Speech. As per the question we have to change it into Indirect Speech. 
 
• The process of transformation as follows: 
 
 
• The given question is an example of an Interrogative sentence. 
 
• 'Said to' will be changed into 'asked'. 
 
• 'If' conjunction will be added to represent whether something is true or not
 
• An interrogative statement is converted into an assertive statement. Thus, the helping verb will be placed after the subject.
 
• 'You' will be changed into 'he'. (Second person->third person)
 
• 'your' will be changed into **'his'.**
 
• 'Have' will be changed into 'had' (Present perfect tense->Past Perfect tense)

 
 
 

Therefore the correct answer is: *The teacher asked the student if he had brought his lunch.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.**

He shall have bought a car.

options.text: A car was being bought by him.
A car was bought by him.
A car will have been bought by him.
A car would have been bought by him.

questions.solution:
**Correct Answer**: A car will have been bought by him. 

The passive voice should use the Future Perfect Tense, as the active voice uses. This is seen only in Sentence 3, which uses ‘will have been’. The other sentences are incorrect due to their wrong tense usage.
